title: Izanami: Death and Separation
subtitle: A return from the underworld is refused

learningObjectives.text: What happens when Izanagi looks at Izanami?
What do the two gods vow at the boulder?

yomi.author: Frank Rinder

yomi.excerpt: he gazed intently into her eyes ere he could recognise her. Izanami was angry that Izanagi had not listened to her commands, for she knew how fruitless would be his efforts. Without the sanction of the ruler of the under-world, she could not return to earth, and this consent she had tried in vain to obtain. Izanagi, hard pressed by the eight monsters who guard the Land of Gloom, had to flee for his life. He defended himself valiantly with his sword; then he threw down his head-dress, and it was transformed into bunches of purple grapes; he also cast behind him the comb, by means of which he had obtained light, and from it sprang tender shoots of bamboo. While the monsters eagerly devoured the luscious grapes and tender shoots, Izanagi gained the broad flight of steps which led back to earth. At the top he paused and cried to Izanami: "All hope of our reunion is now at an end.
yomi.note: Rinder's modern retelling, not a direct Kojiki translation.

narrativeBlocks.title: Into the Land of Gloom
narrativeBlocks.body: Izanagi cannot accept Izanami's death by fire-birth. He descends to Yomi — the Land of Gloom — to beg her to come back to the world they made together.

narrativeBlocks.title: Wait in the dark
narrativeBlocks.body: She agrees to ask the gods of Yomi — but on one condition: he must not look at her. He waits in the darkened hall until patience breaks: he snaps a tooth from his comb, lights it, and looks.

narrativeBlocks.title: The rotting beloved
narrativeBlocks.body: Her body is a mass of maggots and thunder-deities. Shamed beyond forgiveness, she sends the hags of Yomi after him — he slows them by throwing his comb, then grapes, then bamboo shoots, and at last blocks the pass of Yomi with a giant boulder.

narrativeBlocks.title: The divorce spoken through stone
narrativeBlocks.body: Through the boulder Izanami vows: 'I will strangle a thousand of your people every day.' Izanagi answers: 'Then I will cause fifteen hundred to be born.' The world's rates of death and birth are their divorce settlement.

narrativeBlocks.title: Purification begins here
narrativeBlocks.body: Polluted by the land of death, Izanagi washes in a river — and from his washed face are born the week's great gods: Amaterasu from his left eye, Tsukuyomi from his right, Susanoo from his nose. Cleansing makes the gods.

quiz.prompt: What does Izanagi see when he lights his comb-tooth?

choices.text: Izanami's rotting corpse — a mass of maggots and thunder-deities

quiz.explanation: The look breaks her bargain — and earns her eternal rage.

quiz.prompt: What do Izanagi and Izanami vow through the boulder?

choices.text: She will kill a thousand people a day; he will see fifteen hundred born — death and birth as their settlement

quiz.explanation: The world's birth-death balance is fixed by their divorce.
